prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary of the 2019 Conservative Manifesto

This manifesto outlines a governing agenda centred on completing EU withdrawal and domestic investment priorities.

## Core Commitments

The document pledges to finalise EU departure by January, implementing a new trade relationship while maintaining regulatory independence. An Australian-style points-based immigration system would replace freedom of movement, prioritising skilled workers and requiring migrants to contribute before accessing benefits.

## Healthcare

The NHS would receive its largest-ever funding increase, with plans for 50,000 additional nurses, 6,000 more GPs, and 50 million extra annual appointments. Forty new hospitals would be built, alongside cancer diagnostic equipment upgrades. A dedicated NHS visa would fast-track qualified overseas healthcare workers. Mental health treatment would receive equivalent priority to physical health.

## Public Safety

Twenty thousand new police officers would be recruited. Sentencing would be toughened for serious crimes, with automatic halfway release ended for violent offenders. New measures would target knife crime, drug-related offending, and organised crime. Victims would receive enhanced legal protections.

## Education and Skills

Schools would receive £14 billion in additional funding, with minimum per-pupil amounts guaranteed. Teacher starting salaries would rise to £30,000. A £3 billion National Skills Fund would support adult retraining, while further education colleges would receive nearly £2 billion for upgrades.

## Economic Policy

The manifesto commits to no increases in income tax, VAT, or National Insurance rates, while raising the National Insurance threshold. The National Living Wage would increase to £10.50 hourly. Business rates would be reduced following a fundamental review. Corporation tax would remain competitive internationally.

## Infrastructure

Major transport investments include Northern Powerhouse Rail, the Midlands Rail Hub, and nationwide gigabit broadband by 2025. A £28.8 billion roads investment programme would address potholes and improve connections. Electric vehicle charging infrastructure would ensure stations within 30 miles nationwide.

## Housing

The target of 300,000 new homes annually would continue, with infrastructure required before occupation. Measures would help first-time buyers through long-term fixed-rate mortgages. Renters would gain protection through abolished no-fault evictions. Social housing reforms would improve tenant protections.

## Environment

Net zero emissions by 2050 remains the target. Offshore wind capacity would reach 40GW by 2030. Tree planting would increase to 75,000 acres annually. A £640 million Nature for Climate fund would support environmental restoration. Plastic waste exports to non-OECD countries would be banned.

## Regional Development

A Towns Fund would support 100 communities initially. The UK Shared Prosperity Fund would replace EU structural funding. Freeports would be established across all four nations. Devolution would expand, with metro mayors gaining greater transport powers.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

Defence spending would exceed 2% of GDP, increasing above inflation annually. The nuclear deterrent would be maintained. Veterans would receive employment support and legal protections. International development spending would remain at 0.7% of national income.

The manifesto emphasises connecting regions, supporting working families, and maintaining fiscal responsibility while increasing public investment.
